quiz3_WAKE_UP_THAWS_distinction.problem: Proposal describes no marked corresponding FLAIR signal as the WAKE-UP definition. The 2026 primary guideline Table 3 distinguishes WAKE-UP no visible signal change from THAWS no marked change.
quiz3_WAKE_UP_THAWS_distinction.recommended_explanation: An abnormal DWI lesion without visible corresponding FLAIR signal change was the WAKE-UP imaging selection criterion; THAWS allowed no marked FLAIR change. Mismatch supports probabilistic assessment under the appropriate unknown-onset pathway and does not establish an exact onset time or independently determine treatment eligibility. Read DWI with ADC and conventional sequences.

quiz8_CVT_specific_primary_source.recommendation: Retain the haemorrhagic transformation correction and add the 2024 CVT statement for venous thrombosis diagnosis. MRI/MRV or CT/CTV confirms venous occlusion; an AIS guideline alone does not substantiate the venous diagnostic pathway.

other_reviewed_changes: Early normal NCCT does not exclude ischaemic stroke or establish viability.
ASPECTS arithmetic is valid; eligible large predicted-core strokes cannot be universally excluded.
Negative DWI and sequence evolution need conditional wording; fixed individual tissue clocks are unsafe.
CTA and CTP sequence is local-protocol dependent; adjunctive perfusion is not compulsory for all early-window EVT cases.
Mismatch ratio and difference are software estimates under declared thresholds; do not equate printed maps or masks with irreversible histology.
Borderzone mechanism, subacute fogging and collaterals are probabilistic; none independently prescribes treatment or authorizes delay.
Use empty assessment prompts; ASPECTS/no-LVO/normality require actual region and vessel review.
